title: Bayesian computing: exact inference, PyMC and Stan
summary: A complete worked route from probability and exact oracles through actual PyMC computation and self-contained Stan compilation, sampling, diagnostics and decisions.

lessons.title: Generative questions, conditioning and repeated evidence
lessons.outcome: Condition a fault hypothesis on detector signals with Bayes' rule and show why a perfectly repeated signal is not independent new evidence.
lessons.lab: Update the fault probability after one signal, then compare a perfectly repeated reading with two conditionally independent signals.
lessons.verification: Reproduce posterior fault probability 0.692 (odds 2.25) after one signal, the same 0.692 for a duplicated reading and 0.953 for two independent signals.

lessons.title: Log densities, normalization and exact numerical oracles
lessons.outcome: Normalize posterior weights on the log scale, check grid integration against an exact posterior and recover ratios from log densities that underflow.
lessons.lab: Compare grid-integrated posterior moments with their analytic values, then normalize extreme log weights with log-sum-exp.
lessons.verification: Grid mean and variance match the analytic 1.846 and 0.308, and the stable weights for the extreme log densities are about 0.665, 0.245 and 0.090.

lessons.title: Conjugacy, posterior prediction and duplicated observations
lessons.outcome: Derive a beta-binomial posterior predictive distribution, separate parameter uncertainty from outcome variance and show how duplicated records overstate certainty.
lessons.lab: Derive the predictive probabilities for five future trials, then duplicate the observed batch and compare posterior variances.
lessons.verification: Posterior mean 0.714 and predictive variance 1.293 against a plug-in 1.020; duplicating the batch shrinks the parameter variance from 0.0136 to 0.0075.

lessons.title: Probability transformations and Jacobian accounting
lessons.outcome: Change variables in a density with the correct Jacobian and detect the moment error caused by omitting it.
lessons.lab: Verify that a transformed beta density integrates to one, then omit the Jacobian and compare second moments.
lessons.verification: With the Jacobian the transformed density integrates to 1.000 and the second moment is 0.300; omitting it gives 0.333.

lessons.title: Posterior decisions, loss and regret
lessons.outcome: Choose an action by posterior expected utility, contrast it with the posterior probability of benefit and compute each action's expected regret.
lessons.lab: Compute expected net benefit and the probability of positive benefit, then the posterior expected regret of treating and of waiting.
lessons.verification: Expected net benefit 0.714 and probability of benefit 0.781; expected regret 0.137 for treating against 0.852 for waiting selects treatment under the stated utility.

lessons.title: Markov chains, autocorrelation and deceptive acceptance rates
lessons.outcome: Run a Metropolis sampler, estimate an autocorrelation-adjusted effective sample size and show why 100% acceptance can mean no exploration.
lessons.lab: Run a random-walk Metropolis chain on a standard normal target, then set the proposal scale to zero and compare acceptance, mean and variance.
lessons.verification: The working chain has acceptance about 0.70, lag-one correlation 0.78, an AR(1) effective sample size near 300 and variance near 1; the zero-scale chain accepts every move and has variance 0.

lessons.title: Hamiltonian geometry, integration and NUTS motivation
lessons.outcome: Implement leapfrog integration for Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, verify reversibility and energy error, and show how an oversized step destroys acceptance.
lessons.lab: Check leapfrog reversibility and energy error at a small step size, then enlarge the step until the integrator becomes unstable.
lessons.verification: Reversibility error 0 and an energy error near -0.0003 at the small step; the large step produces an enormous energy error and acceptance 0.

lessons.title: Simulation-based calibration and tests that can miss errors
lessons.outcome: Run simulation-based calibration on a conjugate normal model, detect a shifted posterior from its ranks and show that a prior-only algorithm can still pass a rank check.
lessons.lab: Compare rank means for correct, shifted and prior-only inference with 64 posterior draws, then compare their conditional errors.
lessons.verification: Rank means stay near the uniform value 32 for correct (33.0) and prior-only (31.9) inference but fall to 10.6 when shifted; conditional error 0.009 against 0.555 exposes the prior-only algorithm.

lessons.title: An actual PyMC regression and its diagnostic record
lessons.outcome: Fit a small PyMC regression, read its R-hat, bulk effective sample size and divergence record against the conventional screen and generate posterior predictive observations.
lessons.lab: Fit the 16-point regression with two short chains, compare the printed diagnostics with the screen, then sample posterior predictive outcomes.
lessons.verification: Intercept and slope means fall within 0.15 and 0.2 of 0.5 and 1.3, the predictive array has shape (2, 120, 16), and rhat_max, bulk_ess_min and divergences are compared with 1.01, 100 per chain and 0.

lessons.title: Centered and noncentered hierarchical computation
lessons.outcome: Fit centered and noncentered forms of one hierarchy, check group means against a known-hyperparameter shrinkage oracle and compare their diagnostic records.
lessons.lab: Derive the conditional shrinkage oracle, then fit both parameterizations and compare group means, divergences and effective sample sizes.
lessons.verification: The density identity centered + 3 log(tau) = noncentered holds, both fits return finite group means to compare with the oracle (-1.667, 0, 0.962), and each diagnostic record is read against the screen.

lessons.title: Robust likelihoods and predictive criticism
lessons.outcome: Compare normal and Student-t likelihoods on data with one outlier and show how the tail penalty moves the posterior location.
lessons.lab: Fit both likelihoods to eight central points plus an outlier at 8, then compare posterior locations and each model's log-density penalty for the outlier.
lessons.verification: The Student-t posterior location is closer to zero than the normal one; the outlier costs -32.0 log units under the normal against -7.08 under a Student-t with 4 degrees of freedom.

lessons.title: Count models, exposure and overdispersion
lessons.outcome: Fit Poisson and negative-binomial count models, compare predictive dispersion with the observed counts and separate an event rate from its exposure.
lessons.lab: Compare predictive means and variances of both models with the observed counts, then check that rate times exposure determines the Poisson mass.
lessons.verification: Observed mean 4.5 and variance 34.1; the negative-binomial predictive variance exceeds the Poisson one, and rate 2 over exposure 3 gives the same log mass for 4 events as rate 4 over exposure 1.5.

lessons.title: Posterior geometry with weakly identified predictors
lessons.outcome: Derive the exact normal posterior for nearly collinear predictors, compare PyMC coefficient means with it and show that a coefficient sum is far better determined than either coefficient.
lessons.lab: Compute the analytic posterior, fit the same model in PyMC and compare individual coefficient uncertainty with the uncertainty of their sum.
lessons.verification: Sampled coefficient means lie within 0.5 of the analytic posterior; the coefficient correlation is about -0.997 and the posterior SD of the sum (0.037) is far below the individual SDs (about 0.48).

lessons.title: Pointwise predictive evaluation, PSIS and the held-out unit
lessons.outcome: Estimate leave-one-out predictive accuracy with PSIS, compare it with exact refitting and interpret Pareto k against the ArviZ sample-size cutoff.
lessons.lab: Compare PSIS-LOO with exact conjugate refits for a constant and a linear model, then change the predictive unit from single to paired observations.
lessons.verification: Exact LOO favors the linear model, each PSIS error is reported against the exact value, pareto_k_max is compared with the 0.58 cutoff for 240 draws, and the joint two-observation log prediction differs from the product of marginals.

lessons.title: Bayesian resource decisions and Monte Carlo uncertainty
lessons.outcome: Choose an order quantity from a posterior predictive cost, compare a short-chain simulation decision with the exact oracle and report its Monte Carlo regret.
lessons.lab: Optimize the exact negative-binomial predictive cost, then repeat the decision from sampled rates and simulated demand.
lessons.verification: The analytic posterior rate is 3.0 and the exact cost-minimizing quantity is 4 (expected cost 2.866); the simulated choice is within one unit and its regret and maximum cost error are reported.

lessons.title: Gaussian processes and conditional versus integrated uncertainty
lessons.outcome: Match PyMC Gaussian-process predictions with a direct covariance calculation and show how integrating over hyperparameters adds between-component variance.
lessons.lab: Compare the PyMC conditional GP mean and covariance with closed-form kernel algebra, then mix two hyperparameter settings.
lessons.verification: PyMC predictions match the direct calculation within 1e-6, and mixing components with means 0 and 2 and variance 0.1 gives total variance 1.1 rather than the conditional 0.1.

lessons.title: Stan blocks and a conjugate reference model
lessons.outcome: Read the blocks of a Stan program, connect its sampled mean to the conjugate normal posterior and interpret constant versus sampled diagnostic rows.
lessons.lab: Compile and sample the normal-mean model, compare mu with the generated analytic posterior and read the summary rows for constants and for mu.
lessons.verification: posterior_mean 1.905 and posterior_variance 0.190 are constant generated quantities to compare with the sampled mu; mu's R_hat, ESS_bulk and ESS_tail are read against 1.01 and 100 per chain.

lessons.title: Stan matrix regression and typed shape contracts
lessons.outcome: Write a Stan regression with a typed design matrix, follow one observation through the linear predictor and distinguish a new mean from a new outcome.
lessons.lab: Trace one observation through X * beta and the likelihood, then compare the generated new_mean with new_outcome at x = 0.5.
lessons.verification: X has an intercept column and centered x values from -2 to 2, log_lik has one entry per observation, and new_outcome is more dispersed than new_mean because it adds sigma.

lessons.title: Stan constraints, log-rate transformations and Jacobians
lessons.outcome: Compare a declared positive Poisson rate with a manual log-rate parameterization and add the Jacobian that the manual transform needs.
lessons.lab: Sample lambda and z = log(lambda) in one program, then compare both with the exact gamma posterior.
lessons.verification: Both lambda and lambda_from_z should agree with the exact posterior mean 1.333 and variance 0.222 from generated quantities; removing the + z Jacobian term would shift lambda_from_z.

lessons.title: Stan noncentered hierarchies and prediction targets
lessons.outcome: Write a noncentered Stan hierarchy with typed group indices and distinguish predictions for an existing group from predictions for a new group.
lessons.lab: Sample the three-group model, then compare known_group_outcome for group 1 with new_group_mean drawn from the population distribution.
lessons.verification: theta equals mu + tau * z in every draw, draws of new_group_mean are more dispersed than draws of theta[1], and tau, mu and theta are read against the diagnostic screen.

lessons.title: Stan logistic likelihoods and separation-aware priors
lessons.outcome: Fit a Stan Bernoulli-logit model, follow likelihood, fitted probabilities and replicated outcomes, and explain why priors keep coefficients finite under complete separation.
lessons.lab: Sample alpha and beta for the eight-point fixture, read probability, y_rep and probability_at_zero, then reason through a completely separated variant.
lessons.verification: Fitted probabilities rise with x, probability_at_zero equals inv_logit(alpha) in every draw, y_rep holds one binary draw per observation, and beta is read against the diagnostic screen.

lessons.title: Stan marginalized mixtures and label conventions
lessons.outcome: Fit a marginalized two-component normal mixture in Stan with log_mix, fix the label convention with ordered means and compute observation responsibilities.
lessons.lab: Sample the ordered mixture, then compute each observation's responsibility for the first component and replicate observations.
lessons.verification: mu[1] is below mu[2] by construction, the five negative observations have first-component responsibility near 1 and the five positive ones near 0, and log_lik uses log_mix for every observation.

lessons.title: Stan stationary dynamics and multi-step prediction
lessons.outcome: Fit a stationary AR(1) model in Stan including the initial-state distribution and propagate parameter and innovation uncertainty to a three-step forecast.
lessons.lab: Sample mu, phi and sigma, then compare the generated one-step and three-step forecast means, variances and outcomes.
lessons.verification: phi stays inside (-1, 1), horizon_three_variance equals sigma^2 (1 + phi^2 + phi^4) in every draw, and three-step outcomes are more dispersed than one-step outcomes.

lessons.title: Stan censored survival workflow and decision dossier
lessons.outcome: Write censored and left-truncated Weibull AFT likelihood contributions in Stan and report the acceleration factor, hazard ratio, control median and survival at time six.
lessons.lab: Sample the eight-subject censored survival model, then derive the AFT and hazard interpretations of the covariate coefficient.
lessons.verification: acceleration_factor equals exp(beta[2]) and hazard_ratio equals exp(-shape * beta[2]) in every draw; censored rows contribute survival terms and delayed entries condition on survival to entry.
